name: Falmouth Harbour
short_description: Sheltered deep-water harbour on the Fal estuary. Good year-round Bass fishing from the quay walls and excellent Mackerel runs in summer.

name: Newlyn Harbour
short_description: One of England's busiest working fishing harbours. Strong tidal flow outside the breakwater produces reliable Pollack and Wrasse marks.

name: Padstow Harbour
short_description: Picturesque estuary harbour on the Camel. Famous for Flounder and Bass in the estuary channels, with Cod offshore in winter.

name: Looe Harbour
short_description: Charter fishing hub for Shark, Conger Eel, and Bream. The East Looe River mouth is a productive Bass mark on the flood tide.

name: Brixham Harbour
short_description: South Devon trawler port with Torbay providing sheltered inshore marks. Excellent Plaice and Bream grounds within two miles offshore.

name: Dartmouth Harbour
short_description: Deep estuary with strong tidal flow. Mullet shoal under the town pontoon in summer; Bull Huss and Conger in the outer estuary at night.

name: Weymouth Harbour
short_description: Popular charter destination for the Shambles Bank reef. Produces Bream, Plaice, and Turbot; Cod move inshore from November.

name: Poole Quay
short_description: Second-largest natural harbour in the world. Sheltered flats hold Flounder and Bass all year; Poole Bay excellent for evening Bass sessions.

name: Brighton Marina
short_description: Man-made marina with deep access channel. Cod and Whiting in winter from the marina walls; Bass and Garfish in summer around the breakwaters.

name: Whitby Harbour
short_description: North Yorkshire working harbour with outstanding Cod fishing from October to February. Pier fishing produces Codling, Coalfish, and Whiting on night tides.
